findings.native_owner: Venice, Biblioteca Nazionale Marciana, Lat.VI.274 (=2885), ff15v–34r; thesis n396. No direct native collation by this producer.
findings.payload: Ordered names Antonio, Paolo, Francesco, Nicolo.
findings.complete_encoding_summary: Antonio supine on earth; Paolo above tries to cut his testicles; Francesco beats Paolo with a stick; Nicolo separates fighters. Earth-to-upper placement determines recitation order.
findings.limit: Explicit actions join a name sequence; they are not the original remembered proposition. Do not translate the scaffold narrative as original payload.

findings.locators: Thesis pp170–171 n429, native ff23v–24v; explicit index rule n430 f24v.
complete_units: First card eight coins: rich man at first locus paternoster, holding eighth locus object cap. His action may vary.
Second king coins: same rich man at second locus cabbages, crown.
Third knight coins: same rich man at third locus cheese, horse.
Fourth small coins: rich man at fourth locus, kneeling.
Following seven clubs: club bearer with FOUR OR SIX apples; apple is seventh locus object.
Following five cups: drunkard with ONE OR TWO fish; fish is fifth locus object.
findings.incomplete_transition: Quoted Latin then attaches cheese to his sword for three swords without clearly introducing the new swordsman/position. Preserve this excerpt transition gap; do not silently repair it.
findings.unequal_constraint: Held object type encodes its learned position, not number of drawn object instances. Outer locus encodes card serial position, person encodes suit, attribute encodes rank.
findings.limit: This is a worked ordered tuple sequence with encoded relations, not complete narrative verb grammar. No Voynich number/name inferred.

findings.claim: Date, debtor name, father/name family, quantity/units, debit versus credit, living versus deceased father assigned to body parts in fixed order.
findings.limit: Thesis quotes program introduction, not a fully encoded example plus exhaustive bodypart field map. Do not claim complete worked ledger translation; IDEA400 debit-credit precedent remains distinct.
